name: Joe Rogers Jr
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Joe Rogers Jr. is the longtime chairman of Waffle House and the son of one of the 24-hour breakfast chain's cofounders.
There are now 2,100 locations in 25 states and estimated annual revenue of over $1 billion.
He was 26 in 1973 when he took the helm of the chain, which had two family ownership groups, mounting debt and control of only 30% of the locations.
Rogers consolidated ownership within his family, which now has a controlling share, while ending the company's reliance on debt.
Rogers also created an employee ownership plan that now provides 3,500 workers (mostly hourly) with a piece of the business.
forbes_facts: Rogers made a point of keeping his diners defiantly open in the face of calamity and showed up in Charleston in 1989 to pour coffee after Hurricane Hugo hit.
In March 2020, the Waffle House index flashed red as sales dropped 70%, 20% of locations closed and thousands of workers were furloughed.

name: Karim Atiyeh
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Karim Atiyeh is the cofounder and chief technology officer of fintech startup Ramp, which private investors valued at $32 billion in November 2025.
Atiyeh launched the company in 2019 with Eric Glyman and Gene Lee. Each cofounder owns an estimated 6% of Ramp.
Atiyeh and Glyman met as undergrads at Harvard and cofounded their first company, price tracking app Paribus, in 2014.
The pair enrolled Paribus in the elite startup incubator Y Combinator that year and then sold the company to Capital One for an undisclosed sum in 2016.
Atiyeh and Glyman continued to run Paribus as part of Capital One for two and a half years before leaving to launch Ramp.
Before cofounding Paribus, Atiyeh worked for two years at consulting firm Oliver Wyman, doing what he describes as "PowerPoint and Excel".

name: Michael Minhong Yu
sec_insider_companies: New Oriental Education & Technology Group Inc. (EDU) - Director
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Yu Minhong is the founder and chairman of New Oriental Education and Technology Group in Beijing, a provider of educational services.
Also known as Michael Yu, he graduated from Peking University with an English major.
Before starting his own business, Yu was an English instructor at Peking University.

name: Evgeny (Eugene) Shvidler
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2003-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Evgeny Shvidler, who became an American citizen in 1994, is the best friend and a partner of Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.
His core asset is stake in Russian steelmaker Evraz.
Former Executive chairman of Highland Gold Mining, Shvidler sold his 12% stake in this company in 2020.
Shvidler was born in Moscow, Russia. He got an MBA from Fordham University in 1992 and worked for Deloitte & Touche in New York.

Shvidler, a dual British-American citizen, was sanctioned by the U.K. in March 2022. His two jets were detained by British authorities. He filed the claim in 2023 in London to challenge the sanctions.
forbes_facts: His 370-foot yacht, Le Grand Bleu, was a gift from Abramovich.
Shvidler was the primary funder for the rebuilding of a Jewish school in England that is now called Beit Shvidler Primary School.

name: Li Zhiyuan
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Li Zhiyuan chairs Hainan Jinpan Smart Technology, a supplier of energy equipment.
Jinpan went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.
Li worked for most of the 1980s as an engineer at a electric power design institute.

name: Wang Xicheng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Wang Xicheng's fortune rose following the July 2016 IPO of his tire manufacturer, Shandong Linglong Tire, on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Its predecessor was a state-owned tire factory founded in 1975 in Shandong Province.
The company was on the verge of collapse in 1987 when Wang was named leader and shifted its focus to pricier tires.
The company is now a supplier to GM, Ford, Tata, Fiat and Hyundai.

name: Lin Por-Shih
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Lin Por-Shih is the president and CEO of Taiwan Glass, one of Asia's largest glass suppliers.
The company was founded in 1964 by his late father, Lin Yu-Chia, who took it public nine years later.
It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Shih's older brother Por-Fong and younger brother Por-Chun serve as the company's chairman and executive director, respectively.

Por-Shih was indicted by Taipei's local authorities in December 2025 for filing fraudulent business documents in an equity transaction in 2020. Taiwan Glass subsequently made an announcement, claiming it has no impact on the company.

name: Josef Boquoi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2015-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026)
forbes_bio: Frozen-food king Josef Boquoi presides over bofrost, which has approximately 11,000 employees, four million customers and $1.4 billion in revenue.
He joined his father's small coffee- and grain-roasting firm in 1953, after receiving a business degree and completing an apprenticeship in Hamburg.
He founded bofrost in 1966, and its first refrigerated vans hit the streets of Germany in 1969.
He introduced new items and developed a business model based on freezing and packaging a variety of fresh food, and delivering direct to households.
Today, bofrost, based in Straelen, offers upwards of 1,000 different foods in Europe, delivered by a fleet of 5,500 sales vehicles.
forbes_facts: In Venice, customer orders are brought by boat, while in Madrid small vehicles are deployed to be able to navigate through the narrowest of alleys.
Boquoi unsuccessfully sued Germany's Manager Magazine for including him on its list of richest Germans, claiming it was a violation of his privacy.

name: Christian Hymer
forbes_bio: Christian Hymer is the son of Erwin Hymer, founder of the Erwin Hymer Group, a German maker of motor homes.
Hymer owned about half of the company when it was acquired by Thor in 2018 for $1.7 billion.
Erwin Hymer entered the motorhome business in 1956 and sold his first travel trailer, the Weltbummler, a year later.
The company became publicly traded in 1990 and was take private again in 2013.
